messages:
samir: Heads up — legal flagged a clause in the Zenith-14B upstream license. It calls out restrictions on "public hosting" unless attribution is shown and expressly forbids redistribution of model weights (including converted/quantized forms). Can we host this behind our API? Also: customers are asking about getting quantized weights for Dedicated. 

elaine_legal: Quick copy of the clause for context:
```
Clause 5.2: "No public hosting without prominent attribution to Original Authors. Redistribution of model weights, including quantized or converted forms, is prohibited without explicit permission."
```
Short answer: serving the model via our hosted API is typically allowed because we are not distributing weights, but the attribution requirement is real and not just in the repo README. It needs to be prominent in the product where the model output is used, and in developer-facing docs. Shipping quantized weights to customers is likely a redistribution and therefore not permitted without an explicit grant. :warning:

maya_ml: From infra/ops POV — we can definitely keep Zenith-14B as API-only for Hosted and Dedicated (provided weights stay on our infra). For Dedicated: if a customer insists on owning the weights or wants an image with weights, that looks like redistribution. Two options we should standardize on:
1) Hosted + Dedicated: API-only access; dedicated customers get reserved capacity but no weight export.
2) Private/On-prem: if customer runs in their own infra (BYO), they can host under their own contract — but we must ensure licensing checks are done pre-deploy.

Proposed small serve config to make attribution programmatic:
```yaml
serve_config:
  attribution_badge: true   # show persistent badge in Console and SDK playground
  response_headers:
    - X-Model-Attribution: "Zenith-14B — original authors"
  dont_export_weights: true
```

devex-jordan: Clarifying Qs: does "prominent" mean per-completion watermark text, or is a persistent UI badge + About page + API header OK for programmatic users? Also need to know if we must surface this in billing/invoice docs.

elaine_legal: Good Q. Reasonable compliance path is: for interactive web/mobile apps — persistent badge in the UI + About/Legal page mention is sufficient. For programmatic API users we need a response header (as Maya suggested) and a clear line in the developer docs and TOS. We do NOT have to inject the attribution into every generated token/output unless the upstream license explicitly requires it (this one doesn't say per-output).

Also: redistribution clause covers all "derived" weights, including quantized forms, converters, or container images containing weights. So do NOT provide downloadable artifacts that include the weights. You can provide a quantization service run on our infra that returns inference artifacts (like logits) but not the weight files. :no_entry:

sec-bot: FYI security/export-control check — Zenith upstream is in EU. Some downstream deployments into embargoed/high-risk regions may trigger export review. Please route any cross-border Dedicated or Private deployments through SecOps. See: https://redwood/internal/sec-export-guidance :mag:

samir: Thanks — I'll update the model-onboarding checklist with three items: 1) attribution badge + API header required, 2) explicit "no weight export" policy for Hosted/Dedicated, 3) route any Private/deployed-to-certain-regions to SecOps for export review. Opening an infra ticket to add the header + Console badge.

maya_ml: I can add an automated gating check in the onboarding pipeline to assert `dont_export_weights: true` and to inject the X-Model-Attribution header for any Zenith-14B model variant. Will PR tomorrow.

elaine_legal: Awesome — ping me on the PR and I'll sign off on the compliance text we surface in the dev docs. :white_check_mark:

devex-jordan: I'll draft a short snippet for the Quickstart (how to display attribution badge + sample code to read header).

samir: Great — thanks everyone. We'll treat Zen-14B as API-only unless legal grants redistribution rights.
